name: Foreign Subsidies Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: Commission enforcement statistics and self-assessed review only; no independent or causal study of effects on competition, investment or prices
summary: The Foreign Subsidies Regulation lets the Commission check whether subsidies from non-EU governments distort EU takeovers and public tenders. Its first review (July 2026) counted about 100 merger notifications a year, far above the 30-40 expected, a handful of in-depth cases ending in commitments, and several Chinese bidders withdrawing from tenders. No independent study yet measures its effect on competition, investment or prices, and businesses say the filing burden is heavy.

indicators.indicator: Yearly number of cases of alleged distortive foreign subsidies dealt with
indicators.target_or_baseline: IA projected 30-40 merger notifications a year
indicators.evidence: By 31 May 2026: 273 merger notifications (about 100 a year, well above the 30-40 projected), 5,150 submissions across 863 public procurement procedures; 3 in-depth merger and 4 in-depth procurement investigations; ex officio cases opened (e.g. Nuctech, Goldwind).

indicators.indicator: Share of cases found distortive vs total cases
indicators.evidence: About 97% of notified mergers cleared after preliminary review; two merger cases (e&/PPF Telecom, ADNOC/Covestro) and one procurement case ended with commitments; three procurement probes closed after the Chinese bidders withdrew.

indicators.indicator: Share of cases cleared thanks to the balancing test
indicators.evidence: No case has yet applied the balancing test in practice, according to the review.

indicators.objective: Remove distortions caused by foreign subsidies
indicators.indicator: Stakeholder perceptions of the impact of redressive measures
indicators.evidence: Review consultation: stakeholders support the objective but say compliance costs are disproportionate, especially for notifications; Commission plans simplification (higher thresholds, shorter forms). Procurement filing compliance reportedly fell from about 70% to 45% by late 2025.

indicators.indicator: Possible short-term drop in foreign direct investment, offset in the medium term by a level playing field
indicators.evidence: No study measures the FSR's effect on FDI, M&A or tender participation.

literature.citation: European Commission (2021), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on foreign subsidies distorting the internal market (executive summary SWD(2021) 100), SWD(2021) 99
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on foreign subsidies distorting the internal market (executive summary SWD(2021) 100)
literature.outcomes: level playing field; compliance costs; FDI
literature.headline: New instrument with notification for large mergers and tenders; low burden for SMEs; possible short-term drop in FDI offset by fairer competition
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected the new tool to restore fair competition with foreign-subsidised firms at modest cost, while warning that foreign investment might dip at first.

literature.citation: European Commission (2026), Report on the implementation and enforcement of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 (first review, with SWD(2026) 183), COM(2026) 368
literature.title: Report on the implementation and enforcement of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 (first review, with SWD(2026) 183)
literature.method: implementation review (case statistics, consultation, call for evidence)
literature.headline: Fit for purpose; 273 merger notifications to 31 May 2026 (about 100 a year vs 30-40 projected), 97% cleared in preliminary review; 5,150 procurement submissions in 863 procedures; commitments in e&/PPF and ADNOC/Covestro; deterrence via bidder withdrawals; stakeholders report disproportionate costs; targeted simplification planned
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's first review says the regime works and has deterred some subsidised bidders, but handles far more filings than expected and firms complain of heavy paperwork.
